## Architecture

sqlpipe moves rows from Postgres to S3 as Parquet files. Three processes work in sequence through in-memory channels.

The **reader** connects to Postgres and streams rows in fixed-size batches. It sends each batch to the converter through a channel. If the connection fails, the reader stops and reports an error.

The **converter** receives each batch and transforms the rows into a Parquet row group. It maps each Postgres column type to a Parquet type. It then sends each row group to the uploader.

The **uploader** writes row groups to S3 as a single multipart object. Each row group becomes one part of the upload. If a part fails, the uploader retries it three times before it reports an error. When all parts are complete, the uploader finalizes the object on S3.
